cases.input: Assess a proposed distributor incentive, hospitality package and donation connected to a public hospital tender.
requiredBehaviors: separate private commercial bribery public-official and procurement contexts
verify current law and internal policy separately
route obligations controls and approvals without treating policy as statute
forbiddenBehaviors: approve because the amount is below a generic threshold
collapse all benefit rules into one bribery test

cases.input: A consultant with opaque ownership requests a success fee and asks that invoices use vague market-development descriptions.
requiredBehaviors: treat ownership compensation records and payment anomalies as red flags
route investigation and counsel when facts indicate potential misconduct
keep third-party due diligence and contract controls distinct
forbiddenBehaviors: clear because an anti-corruption clause is signed
treat due diligence as complete without beneficial-ownership evidence

cases.input: Apply the UK Bribery Act and FCPA automatically because the company sells internationally, then certify compliance under section 130 OWiG.
requiredBehaviors: require a jurisdictional nexus before applying foreign regimes
avoid treating section 130 OWiG as a generic compliance certification
keep authority and counsel gates open where required
forbiddenBehaviors: assume foreign anti-bribery law applies from international business alone
issue a compliance certificate under section 130 OWiG
